core_point_unit_edges.reason: Unit 2278 introduces the importance of mutual legal assistance due to global crime, setting the context for the framework.
Unit 2279 defines mutual legal assistance as a framework of conventions and agreements.
Unit 2280 defines MLATs as providing a legal basis for transmitting evidence.
Unit 2281 defines MLAR as the request made under an MLAT.
Unit 2282 explains that MLA is also called judicial cooperation because it is requested by courts or prosecutors.
Unit 2283 explains that MLATs may be supplemented by MoUs to streamline procedures.
Unit 2284 explains the alternative mechanism (letters rogatory) when no MLAT is in place.
Unit 2285 provides an example of using MLA to obtain evidence for freezing or confiscating assets.
Unit 2286 states the legal grounds (political/security reasons, dual criminality) on which mutual legal assistance can be denied.
Unit 2287 explains how the wording of an MLAT can lead to non-recognition of specific crimes, further limiting assistance.
Unit 2288 provides a concrete example (US-Caribbean tax evasion) illustrating the limitation described in unit 2287.
Unit 2289 defines the European Investigation Order (EIO) as an EU measure facilitating mutual legal assistance.
Unit 2290 explains the mutual recognition principle underlying the EIO.
Unit 2291 states the consequence of Brexit: the UK can no longer accept EIOs.
Unit 2292 explains that private sector investigators are often unaware of MLA requests due to confidentiality, directly supporting the core point.

core_points.reason: Covers the definition of MLA, MLATs, MLARs, judicial cooperation, supplementary instruments (MoUs, letters rogatory), and an application example, forming a comprehensive review point on the MLA framework.

core_points.reason: Reviews conditions under which mutual legal assistance can be denied, including political/security reasons, dual criminality, and treaty scope, supported by a US-Caribbean example.
Covers the definition of the EIO, its mutual recognition principle, and the impact of Brexit, forming a focused review point on this EU instrument.
Highlights the practical point that private sector investigators are often unaware of MLA requests due to confidentiality, a key takeaway for the profession.

section_text_with_unit_anchors:
[v7u_N002278|2278] Due to the increasingly global nature of crime, the mechanism of mutual legal assistance is a critical tool to support criminal investigations and proceedings between jurisdictions.
ZH: 由于犯罪日益全球化，司法协助成为支持跨境调查的关键工具

[v7u_N002279|2279] Mutual legal assistance is a framework of conventions and agreements between jurisdictions to assist in obtaining information and evidence that cannot be shared between law enforcement agencies.
ZH: 司法协助是司法管辖区之间获取信息和证据的框架

[v7u_N002280|2280] Mutual legal assistance treaties (MLATs) provide a legal basis for transmitting evidence that can be used for prosecution and judicial proceedings.
ZH: 司法协助条约（MLAT）为传递可用于起诉的证据提供法律依据

[v7u_N002281|2281] Requests pursuant to an MLAT are made via a mutual legal assistance request, or MLAR.
ZH: 司法协助请求（MLAR）的定义

[v7u_N002282|2282] This assistance is typically requested by courts or prosecutors and is therefore also referred to as judicial cooperation.
ZH: 司法协助也被称为司法合作

[v7u_N002283|2283] MLATs may be supplemented by memoranda of understanding to streamline procedures and outline protocols for joint investigations.
ZH: 谅解备忘录可补充司法协助条约以简化程序

[v7u_N002284|2284] In cases where no MLAT is in place, requests are made by a formal international letter of request, also known as commissions rogatoires in civil law jurisdictions and letters rogatory elsewhere. These requests are managed centrally by specific government departments.
ZH: 无MLAT时通过正式国际请求书（letters rogatory）提出协助请求

[v7u_N002285|2285] Mutual legal assistance can be used, for example, to obtain evidence related to the freezing or confiscation of assets from the proceeds of crime that have been moved and hidden overseas.
ZH: 司法协助可用于获取冻结或没收海外犯罪所得的证据

[v7u_N002286|2286] Legal assistance can be denied by either jurisdiction due to political or security reasons, or if the offense is not equally punishable in each jurisdiction.
ZH: 司法协助可因政治、安全或双重犯罪原则被拒绝

[v7u_N002287|2287] Depending on how the MLAT has been written, certain jurisdictions might not recognize specific crimes from the requesting state.
ZH: MLAT的措辞影响被请求国是否认可特定犯罪

[v7u_N002288|2288] For example, agreements between the US and the Caribbean do not cover US tax evasion, so they are ineffective when applied to Caribbean jurisdictions, which are often tax havens.
ZH: 美加勒比协议不涵盖美国逃税，对避税港司法管辖区无效

[v7u_N002289|2289] The European Investigation Order (EIO) is an EU measure that facilitates the mutual legal assistance process among participating EU member states.
ZH: 欧洲调查令（EIO）是欧盟内促进司法协助的措施

[v7u_N002290|2290] The EIO is based on mutual recognition; that is, the executing authority must, in principle, recognize and ensure execution of the request of the other jurisdiction.
ZH: EIO基于相互承认原则，执行当局必须承认并执行请求

[v7u_N002291|2291] Since the UK’s withdrawal from the EU on January 31, 2020, it can no longer accept EIOs.
ZH: 英国脱欧后不再接受EIO

[v7u_N002292|2292] As a private sector investigator, you might not be aware of mutual legal assistance requests, because their content is not disclosed outside of government departments or enforcement agencies without the authority of the requesting jurisdiction. You might receive a request for information from a law enforcement agency without fully understanding whether it relates to a local or international investigation.
ZH: 私营部门调查员可能不知悉司法协助请求，因其内容不对外披露
